newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares up in technical correction.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares up in technical correction.

text.p: Israeli shares rose on Monday in what traders said was a technical correction following two days of heavy losses sparked by political uncertainty.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.32 percent, or 2.44 points, to 186.72. The Maof 25 index gained 1.46 percent to 195.90.
Closing volume was not available because trading of shares in the Karam index of small cap stocks was continuing.
The Tel Aviv bourse will close two hours early throughout the week due to the Jewish holiday of Succoth. Normal trading hours will resume on October 6.

"What we saw today was only a technical correction following the sharp declines of Thursday and Sunday. The mood is still very negative and investors hope the planned summit in Washington will eventually take place," said Julien Assous at Sahar Securities.

"Everything depends now on the outcome of the summit. Despite today's rise activity was very low. Most of the foreign investors remained sidelined although some of them started buying today, but only in specific shares," Assous said.
Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat asked U.S. President Bill Clinton to postpone the Middle East summit set for Tuesday and Wednesday in Washingon.
"Investors are more optimistic now. The reaction to the clashes last week was too sharp. Prices are very cheap now and the mood is improving," said Amir Eayal at Epsilon Securities.
Israel's opening of a tunnel near Moslem shrines in East Jerusalem last week sparked clashes in which 55 Palestinians and 14 Israelis were killed.
Africa Israel Investments rose 4.5 percent to 394,765 for no evident reason.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which rose 1.50 percent to 147,644 on turnover of 7.0 million shekels; Koor Industries, which gained 2.75 percent to 28,454 on turnover of 2.4 million shekels; and Super Sol which gained 0.75 percent to 7,318 on volume of 2.2 million shekels.
